sections.title: Rosette and flowering stem
sections.text: This Chilean bromeliad forms a basal rosette of stiff, spiny leaves up to about 1 m long. The flowering panicle can reach about 5 m; its trumpet-shaped flowers are lime-green to turquoise. The flowering rosette dies after blooming, while offsets may persist.

sections.title: Pollination and safety
sections.text: Birds feed on nectar at the base of the flowers in its native range. The leaf margins bear sharp spines; human edibility or toxicity was not established in the sources consulted.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.text: Like Puya alpestris, it is a spiny Chilean rosette bromeliad; its green to turquoise flowers differ from the blue-green flowers of P. alpestris.
